lit.\u0027¿Cuál NO puede ser donor de H?\u00: "Which one can NOT be an H donor?"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003ePuente de H\u003c/b\u: "H bond: H–O/N···:O/N. Alcohol and 1°/2° amine: donor and acceptor."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003ealcoh:
"

The alcohol is a very weak acid (pKa ≈ 16), is oxidized, dehydrates with H₂SO₄ and its OH is substituted with HX (protonated as a good leaving group). The ether is hardly reactive (that is why it is used as a solvent) and is only cleaved by concentrated HI/HBr. The amine is a base and nucleophile: it is alkylated, acylated and forms salts. Compare them in the “Graphs” matrix.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl grupo polar forma:
"

The polar group forms H bonds with water (hydrophilic), whereas the hydrocarbon chain (hydrophobic) breaks them without compensation. Result: methanol, ethanol and propan-1-ol are miscible with water; solubility drops to 7.4 g/100 mL (butanol), 2.2 (pentanol), 0.6 (hexanol). Low-weight amines are soluble; those with more than 6 C, little.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl O (χ = 3,5) y el N:
"

O (χ = 3.5) and N (3.0) are more electronegative than C (2.5): the C–O, C–N, O–H and N–H bonds are polar and the molecules have a dipole moment (μ): propane 0.08 D · dimethyl ether 1.30 D · ethanol 1.69 D · propylamine 1.17 D. Dipole–dipole intermolecular forces explain much of their properties; but the most important factor is the ability to form hydrogen bonds.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLas aminas son \u003c:
"

Amines are weak bases and nucleophiles thanks to the lone pair on N. Strength is compared with the pKa of the conjugate acid (pKaH): NH₃ 9.25 · CH₃NH₂ 10.62 · (CH₃)₂NH 10.73 · (CH₃)₃N 9.80. Alkyl groups donate electrons and stabilize the cation; in aqueous phase the 3° amine loses out through solvation and hindrance. Aniline (pKaH 4.6) is much less basic because the lone pair is delocalized into the ring.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara masas molares pa:
"

For similar molar masses (≈ 46 g/mol): propane −42 °C (dispersion only) · dimethyl ether −25 °C (dipole) · ethanol +78 °C (strong H bonds). 1° and 2° amines boil between ethers and alcohols: propylamine (48 °C) versus propan-1-ol (97 °C). Trimethylamine (3 °C), with no N–H, boils much lower than its isomers.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003epuent:
"

A hydrogen bond links an H attached to O or N (donor) with the lone pair of another O or N (acceptor); the energy is ≈ 15–30 kJ/mol, between a covalent bond and dispersion forces. Alcohols are donors and acceptors; 1° and 2° amines too (weaker because N is less electronegative); ethers and 3° amines are only acceptors and do not associate with each other.

"
